site.name: Balmoral
site.location: About 900 feet east of Boulder Falls, Boulder County Tungsten Mining District
overview: The Balmoral Mine was a historic tungsten mine in Boulder County, about 900 feet east of Boulder Falls.
State and federal mining records document production, two connected shafts, multiple underground levels, and development on the Balmoral and Smith veins.

timeline.text: A detailed mine map of the Balmoral property was prepared for the Colorado Tungsten Corporation, documenting the property during the World War I-era tungsten-mining period.
USGS Professional Paper 245 records the mine as owned by Mrs. Washburn of Sugar Loaf and being worked by Hurlburt and Vant.
Colorado's Tungsten Mines of Colorado inventory reported about 1,500 units of production and summarized the mine's shafts, levels, veins, and remaining exploration potential.

moreHistory: The 1960 Colorado mine inventory places Balmoral in the southwest quarter of Section 36, Township 1 North, Range 72 West, about 900 feet east of Boulder Falls. It describes an inclined main shaft with levels at 16, 39, and 79 feet and a second shaft about 70 feet northeast that connected with the 39-foot level; both shafts were reported caved by that time.

USGS Professional Paper 245 reports that a stope at the shaft on the first level was said to have produced about $16,000 worth of ore, while another stope to the southwest yielded lower-grade material. Published records identify mineralization on the Balmoral and Smith veins.

The mapped identification point near 40.00667, -105.39806 is used as a site-level reference consistent with published Boulder County tungsten-district locality records and the documented position east of Boulder Falls. It should not be interpreted as a field-surveyed surviving shaft collar, property boundary, or statement of current access.
